chain.label: No formal ENG operating procedures; stations assigned pilots joint flying and reporting duties
chain.trigger: Contributing to the accident was the lack of formal procedures for Phoenix-area ENG pilots to follow regarding the conduct of these operations.

chain.label: Six helicopters maneuvering close-in over a moving pursuit within a narrow low-level altitude band
chain.trigger: In addition to the channel 3 and 15 helicopters and the police helicopter, three other ENG helicopters were operating in the airspace over the police pursuit.

caused_by.evidence: the FAA should develop LOAs or amend existing LOAs to specify minimum horizontal and vertical aircraft separation requirements

chain.label: Low helicopter conspicuity: no high-visibility rotor blade paint or high-intensity anticollision lights
chain.trigger: The accident helicopters were not equipped with LED anticollision lights and did not have high-visibility blade paint on their main rotor blades.

chain.label: Pilots never reconciled their identical 2,000-foot altitude and stopped coordinating positions 4 minutes before impact
chain.trigger: neither pilot recognized each other's intention to operate at the same altitude

caused_by.evidence: evidence indicated that these procedures were not rigorously followed on the day of the accident

chain.label: Both pilots narrated the developing carjacking, diverting attention to the ground in the final minute
chain.trigger: the pilots were continuously reporting the events as they unfolded, which narrowed the pilots' attention to the ground and away from other tasks, such as maintaining the helicopters' stated position and altitude and scanning the area for potential collision hazards

caused_by.evidence: Contributing to this failure was the pilots' responsibility to perform reporting and visual tracking duties to support their station's ENG operation.

chain.label: Both pilots failed to see and avoid the other helicopter; one or both lost awareness of its position
chain.trigger: the probable cause of this accident was both pilots' failure to see and avoid the other helicopter

caused_by.evidence: the channel 3 and 15 pilots' reporting and visual tracking duties immediately before the collision likely precluded them from recognizing the proximity of their helicopters at that time

these transmissions, which occurred about 4 minutes before the midair collision, were the last times that the channel 3 and 15 pilots coordinated their helicopter's position or their intentions with each other
a high-visibility paint scheme on the helicopters' main rotor blades or high-visibility anticollision lights could have facilitated the detection of the impending collision risk
this accident demonstrates the limitations of the see-and-avoid concept for reliably ensuring separation of aircraft during high-density traffic operations

chain.label: Both helicopters turned right and changed altitude while tracking the suspect, eroding separation
chain.trigger: After completing 90 degree turns, the helicopters appeared to be closer in proximity than before

caused_by.evidence: at some point the channel 3 helicopter's altitude increased, the channel 15 helicopter's altitude decreased, or both
The additional tasks of directly observing activities on the ground and providing narration could have affected the pilots' ability to maintain their helicopter's position

chain.label: Main rotor blades of the two helicopters struck each other about 1246:18
chain.trigger: the yellow blade on the left side of the channel 3 helicopter and the red blade on the right side of the channel 15 helicopter contacted each other about 2 feet from the end of each blade and then separated

caused_by.evidence: the accident helicopters were initially positioned apart at a reasonable distance but had moved closer together after the police announcement of the carjacking
the channel 3 and 15 helicopters collided because one or both pilots lost awareness of the other helicopter's position

chain.label: Channel 3 rotor severed its tail boom and the helicopter fragmented in flight; channel 15 pitched nose down
chain.trigger: the helicopter then fragmented in the air and struck the ground in an inverted position

caused_by.evidence: After the outboard section of the channel 3 yellow blade separated, that helicopter's main rotor blades deformed and broke the helicopter's tail boom into several pieces

chain.label: Both helicopters struck the ground in a park and were destroyed by impact and postcrash fire
chain.trigger: the helicopters were destroyed by impact forces and postcrash fire

caused_by.evidence: that helicopter entered a nose-down attitude, which it maintained until impacting the ground
The main wreckages from both helicopters were located about 160 feet apart in a park.

chain.label: All four occupants of the two helicopters were killed
chain.trigger: The occupants on board both helicopters were killed

caused_by.evidence: the cause of death for the ENG pilots and photographers was multiple blunt force injuries
